questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: A study finding little link between tech and teens' mental health
How parents can stop their children watching so much television
Why video games are bad for young people's eyes
How many TV channels there were in the past
questions.why: Sam says they'll look at a report which finds little evidence linking technology with mental health problems in adolescents.

questions.q: What do Neil and Sam think about teenagers and technology at the start?
options: They both think it is very harmful
They both think it is completely safe
Neil is worried, but Sam thinks it isn't all bad
Sam is worried, but Neil thinks it is fine
questions.why: Neil says he's not convinced about the report, while Sam says 'I don't think it's all bad news'.

questions.q: How is today's technology different from television, according to Sam?
options: It is much cheaper than a television
It is only used at school
It is less colourful
It is interactive and social
questions.why: Sam says unlike passive TV, today's technology is interactive and connects teenagers to friends.

questions.q: How many teenagers did the Oxford Internet Institute study look at?
options: About 4,000
Around 40,000
Four million
questions.why: The study analysed data from over 400,000 British and American teenagers.

questions.q: Why wasn't Ghislaine Boddington expecting to find clear proof of harm?
options: She thinks teenagers are quite savvy with tech
She thinks the study was badly done by the researchers
Teenagers don't use technology very much
She doesn't know any teenagers
questions.why: She says teenagers are 'much more savvy than many adults think'.

questions.q: What example does Ghislaine give of teenagers using technology sensibly?
options: They turn off their phones completely every night
They only use social media at weekends and on holidays
They let their parents check their phones every evening
They use app blockers and know about addictive design
questions.why: She says the teenagers she knows have app blockers and are aware of the addiction problem.

questions.q: According to the presenters, why is reducing screen time important?
options: Because screens seriously damage young people's eyesight
Because teachers want students to do more homework at home
Because many games and social media are made to be addictive
Because phones and tablets use too much electricity at night
questions.why: Neil says most video games and social media are 'designed for addiction'.

questions.q: What does Dr Matti Vuorre suggest about young people who grow up with devices?
options: They are more likely to become addicted to screens
They are naturally skilled at using it well
They find it hard to talk to people face to face
They should wait longer before getting a phone
questions.why: He says it's not a surprise that digital natives are skilled in using technology to their benefit.
